guide.title: Manele Golf Course: Golf on Lānaʻi, Hawaii
guide.intro: Golf Digest's Best in State 2025-'26 ranking for Hawaii places Manele Golf Course second and labels it "Public." Four Seasons Resort Lanai, which operates the course, states on two of its own pages: "Course access is not available for day guest use." Those two named sources disagree, and on the evidence either one publishes, a visitor who is not staying at the resort cannot play this course. This guide says so here and again in the FAQ. The course sits at Four Seasons Resort Lanai on the island of Lānaʻi, in the County of Maui — Hawaii records zero incorporated places in every Census vintage, so the island, not a city, is the honest locality, and County of Maui, the jurisdiction's own name for itself, is the governing one. Having said what a non-resort visitor cannot do, this guide then turns to Kapalua: Plantation, on Maui, as the round such a visitor can actually book.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Lānaʻi has no road or bridge connection to another island; a visitor reaches it by air or by sea. Hawaii Department of Transportation's own site describes Lanai Airport (LNY), on Airport Road, Lanai City, HI 96763, as an airport "served by interisland planes." By sea, Expeditions operates the Maui–Lānaʻi ferry across the ʻAuʻau Channel, on the route Māʻalaea, Maui, to Mānele, Lānaʻi, and back; the ferry lands at Mānele, the same bay the golf course sits above. By road, Lanai Airport is 10.8 miles from Four Seasons Resort Lanai — a road distance, not a straight-line one. Hawaii carries zero incorporated places statewide in every Census TIGERweb vintage (against 483 in California, 149 in Alaska and 8 in Rhode Island); the state instead carries 163 census-designated places, among them Lanai City, the CDP nearest the course and the mailing address the Census geocoder returns for it. The county-equivalent is County of Maui, the jurisdiction's own name for itself on its site, its address block, its footer and its charter's cover page.

sections.heading: Manele Golf Course
sections.body: Golf Digest's Best in State list for Hawaii, 2025-'26, ranks Manele Golf Course second and labels it "Public" — corroborated by the same ranking page's own embedded data (displayedFacilityType "Public," private: false, facilityType "Daily Fee") and by Golf Digest's course page, which records "Best in State: Ranked second, 2021 to current" and, on its current page, "2025-'26 ranking (and previous): 2nd." Only one course ranks above it: Nanea Golf Club, which Golf Digest labels "Private." Four Seasons Resort Lanai, which operates Manele Golf Course, publishes hours of Tuesday through Sunday, 8:00 a.m. first tee to 6:00 p.m., and the course is closed Mondays. The resort's own pages, fetched live, state that Manele Golf Course will be closed for aeration 21 to 28 September 2026, 29 March to 4 April 2027, and 20 to 27 September 2027, and that "Special post-aeration rates are available" — no figure is given.

sections.heading: Who can play here
sections.body: Golf Digest labels Manele Golf Course "Public." Four Seasons Resort Lanai, which operates it, states on two of its own pages: "Course access is not available for day guest use." On the golf-experience page, that sentence is immediately preceded by "Preferred tee times, complimentary food and beverages, and our warm aloha spirit ensure a memorable day – or days – on the greens" — the "or days" naming the multi-day stay the sentence assumes. Club rentals are described as complimentary "for resort guests playing 9- or 18-hole rounds after 12:00 noon," scoped to resort guests. The resort's one unlimited-golf product, "Member for a Week," is sold as "unlimited golf for one player at any time during a seven-day stay" — the unit of access is a stay, not a round. The resort publishes no green-fee page, no tee-time booking page and no non-guest rate; the only published routes to the course are a telephone line, +1 (808) 565-2000, and a chat widget, both offered as a concierge service for guests rather than a public tee sheet. On this evidence, a visitor who is not staying at Four Seasons Resort Lanai cannot play Manele Golf Course, and this guide does not say otherwise.

sections.heading: Kapalua: Plantation, the practical round
sections.body: For a visitor who is not staying at Four Seasons Resort Lanai, Golf Digest's same Hawaii list points to a different course. Kapalua: Plantation, in Lahaina, ranks third on the 2025-'26 Best in State list and carries the same "Public" label; Kapalua fields two ranked courses on the list, Plantation at third and Bay at nineteenth. Kapalua: Plantation is on Maui, not on Lānaʻi — a visitor reaches it by crossing the ʻAuʻau Channel on the Expeditions ferry, from Mānele, Lānaʻi, to Māʻalaea, Maui, or by flying into one of Maui's own airports. This guide makes no claim about Kapalua: Plantation's green fee, tee-time policy or hours; no source verified for this guide reaches that course's own booking pages.

faq.question: Can a visitor who is not a resort guest play Manele Golf Course?
faq.answer: No, on the evidence Four Seasons Resort Lanai itself publishes. Golf Digest labels the course "Public," but the resort states on two of its own pages, "Course access is not available for day guest use." The resort publishes no green-fee page, no tee-time booking page and no non-guest rate; the only published routes to the course are its telephone line, +1 (808) 565-2000, and a chat widget, both offered as a concierge service for resort guests.

faq.question: Is Manele Golf Course public or private?
faq.answer: Golf Digest's own label is "Public," and its embedded ranking data records the same: displayedFacilityType "Public," private: false, facilityType "Daily Fee." Four Seasons Resort Lanai, which operates the course, states on two of its own pages that "Course access is not available for day guest use." Both statements are quoted here rather than reconciled, because the sources themselves disagree: a labelled-Public course that excludes anyone not staying at the resort.

faq.question: When is Manele Golf Course closed?
faq.answer: The resort's own pages state the course will be closed for aeration 21 to 28 September 2026, 29 March to 4 April 2027, and 20 to 27 September 2027, with special post-aeration rates and no figure published. The course is also closed every Monday; published hours are Tuesday through Sunday, 8:00 a.m. first tee to 6:00 p.m.

faq.question: How do I get to Lānaʻi?
faq.answer: By air, into Lanai Airport (LNY), which Hawaii's Department of Transportation describes as "served by interisland planes." By sea, on the Expeditions ferry, which runs the route Māʻalaea, Maui, to Mānele, Lānaʻi, and back, across the ʻAuʻau Channel; the ferry lands at Mānele, the same bay the golf course sits above.

faq.question: I can't book a tee time at Manele — where else can I play?
faq.answer: Kapalua: Plantation, in Lahaina, on Maui — not on Lānaʻi. It ranks third on the same Golf Digest Hawaii 2025-'26 list and carries the same "Public" label. A visitor reaches it by crossing the ʻAuʻau Channel on the Expeditions ferry or by flying into one of Maui's own airports. This guide does not establish Kapalua: Plantation's green fee, tee-time policy or hours.

faq.question: What county is Manele Golf Course in?
faq.answer: County of Maui — the jurisdiction's own name for itself, on its site, its address block, its footer and its charter's cover page. "Maui County" is the Census Bureau's own label for the same jurisdiction, not its self-name. Hawaii has no incorporated places in any Census vintage, so County of Maui is the governing jurisdiction here rather than a city.
